DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilq.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 11 s. 2021 4 February 2021 MR. AUDIEMUR CABELTES ZAYAS Bonifacio St., Brgy. Upper Jasaan Jasaan, Misamis Oriental Dear Mr. Zayas: This has reference to your letter, concerning the validity/legality of Jasaan Municipal Ordinance No. 123-2019, entitled "An Ordinance Providing for Water Rates, Rules and Regulations Relative to the Operation of LGU-Jasaan Water Supply System and for other Purposes" (hereinafter referred to as the "Ordinance"). Per your letter and its attachments, the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) of Jasaan, Misamis Oriental enacted the aforesaid Ordinance on 2 December 2019. On 11 May 2020, the SB of Jasaan passed Municipal Ordinance No. 129-2020 entitled "An Ordinance Amending by Deleting the Word 'To Two (2) Years' in Section 21 (Penal Provision) of the Municipal Ordinance No. 123-2019 Entitled "An Ordinance Providing for Water Rates, Rules and Regulations Relative to the Operation of LGU- Jasaan Water Supply System and for other Purposes". On 29 June 2020, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Misamis Oriental passed Resolution No. 506-2020 entitled "Resolution Declaring as valid Ordinance No. 129-2020 of Jasaan, Misamis Oriental Entitled "An Ordinance Amending by Deleting the Word "To Two (2) Years" in Section 21 (Penal Provision) of the Municipal Ordinance No. 123-2019 Entitled "An Ordinance Providing for Water Rates, Rules and Regulations Relative to the Operation of LGU- Jasaan Water Supply System and for other Purposes". Hence, your query on the validity/legality of the subject ordinance in question.

As can be gleaned from your letter, you are of the view that the subject ordinance is tainted with various non-conformities and/or abnormalities. Your remonstrations can be reduced to the following essential arguments, thus: 1. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan (SP) concerned should have declared MO No. 123-2019 to be valid after the corrections initiated by the passage of MO 129-2020. Section 56 of RA 716() otherwise known as the Local Government Code requires review of municipal ordinances or resolutions by the SP for scrutiny and approval as to validity as well as determine whether such ordinance is within the scope of the prescribed powers of the sanggunian. Interestingly, two (2) SB ordinances were submitted for review, MO No. 123-2019 and MO No. 129- 2020 but only the latter was declared valid; 2. Permit/ Authority from the National Water Resources Board (NWRB) is a necessary requirement before water is appropriated; 3. No proof of conduct that appropriate consultations were done prior to the enactment of the subject ordinance in question; and 4. The provisions surrounding the passage of MO No 123- 2019 is tainted with blatant inconsistencies and irregularities Foremost, please be apprised that this Department, in its previous legal opinions, has been consistent that inasmuch as the ordinance has undergone the procedural process for its enactment pursuant to the Local Government Code of 1991 (Code), the same is considered valid unless declared otherwise by courts. Accordingly, this Department is bereft of authority to rule on the legality of the subject ordinance in question as this is within the jurisdiction of the regular courts. Moreover, pursuant to this Department's Memorandum Order No. 2010-02 dated 17 September 2010, it provides: "xxx all concerned are hereby advised that the Department shall not act on queries of the following kinds, to wit: Those presumptively valid acts; e.g., enacted ordinance. consummated acts that alreadv eniov the

presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, and similar instances; Xxx (Emphasis supplied) Thus, any issues concerning the legality of an ordinance shall be threshed out by the proper court. Notwithstanding, for purposes of academic discussion, we shall discuss the laws applicable on the issues posed as well as previous interpretations of the Department on the matter. On the first issue, herein petitioners contend that MO No. 123-2019 cannot be implemented "in view of its various unconformities (sic) as well as blatant irregularities and inconsistencies". While the Code requires review of municipal ordinances by the SP for scrutiny and approval vis-å-vis the validity of such ordinances, it also provides reglementary period within which SP shall take an action on the review of ordinances. Section 56 of the Code provides, viz: "Section 56. Review of Component City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. If no action has been taken by the sangguniang panlalawigan within thirty (30) days after submission of such an ordinance or resolution, the same shall be presumed consistent with law and therefore valid." (Emphasis supplied) Based on the foregoing, the law provides reglementary period within which SP shall take an action on the review of ordinances, which is thirty (30) days after submission of the same. It is worthwhile stressing that such period should be reckoned from the date of the submission of ordinance, and not from the submission of the requested documents/reports of the reviewing SP. Accordingly, if SP had taken no action on the review of the subject municipal ordinance within 30 days after it was submitted, the law expressly provides that such ordinance is presumed consistent with law and therefore valid. This Department, in its previous opinions, had consistently opined that the phrase 'take action" should be construed as either approval or disaooroval of the ordinance and not iust anv other action of the reviewina

sanggunian, such as referral to a committee. After the lapse of such period, and no official and/or formal document, such as a resolution which shall contain the findings of the SP on review of the SB ordinance, was issued by the SP, it can be validly stated that the SP failed to act within thirty (30) days and the ordinance under review can be presumed consistent with law and therefore valid. Therefore, an ordinance is deemed valid upon failure of the SP to declare the same invalid within 30 days after its submission, notwithstanding any legal defect imputed against it thereafter. Anent the second issue, a permit/authority from the National Water Resources Board (NWRB) is necessary before water is appropriated pursuant to Presidential Decree (PD) No. 1067 otherwise known as the 'Water Code of the Philippines". Section 1 of its Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR), as amended, in relation to Section 2 thereof respectively provide: "Section 1. Water may be appropriated for the following descending purposes and uses: Xxx b. Municipal Use of water for municipal; purposes is the utilization of water for supplying the water requirements of a community, whether by piped or bulk distributing for domestic and other uses, direct consumption, the drawer or abstractor of which being the national government, its subsidiary agencies, local government units, private persons, cooperatives or corporations. Section 2. When Permit/Authority from the National Water Resources Board Must be Secured- As required under the provisions of PD 1067 a permit/authority shall be secured from the Board in the following instances: Appropriation of water for any purpose stated under Section I, except for "purely domestic purpose" In regard to the third issue, insofar as the issue on consultation or public hearings is concerned, it is worthwhile to note that Section 2 (c) of the Code pertains to national governments and not the local government units. Nonetheless, it would not be amiss to note that public hearings are conducted by legislative bodies to allow interested parties to ventilate their views on a proposed law or ordinance. These views, however, are not binding on the legislative body and it is not compelled by law to adopt the same. Sanggunian members are elected by the people to make laws that

will promote the general interest of their constituents. They are mandated to use their discretion and best judgment in serving the people. Parties who participate in public hearings to give their opinions on a proposed ordinance should not expect that their views would be patronized by their lawmakersl. As to the fourth issue, insofar as the absence of an IRR is concerned, the promulgation of an IRR is not a prerequisite for the effectivity of an ordinance. Under the Code, the effectivity of an ordinance is determined not upon the issuance of its IRR but rather on the date as indicated in the ordinance itself. In the absence of an express date, the same shall be operative after ten (10) days from the date a copy of such ordinance is posted in a bulletin board at the entrance of the municipal hall and in at least two (2) other conspicuous places in the municipality. In DILG LO No. 5 series of 2018 dated 25 January 2018, we opined, thus: "Effectivity is the time by which an ordinance is made effective and can already be implemented and given full force and effect. Effectivity is governed by Section 59 (a) of the Local Government Code of 1991, thus: "Section 59. Effectivity of Ordinances or Resolutions. - (a) Unless otherwise stated in the ordinance or the resolution approving the local development plan and public investment program, the same shall take effect after ten (IO) days from the date a copy thereof is posted in a bulletin board at the entrance of the provincial capitol or city, municipal, or barangay hall, as the case may be, and in at least two (2) other conspicuous places in the local government unit concemed. " Based on Section 59 (a) of the Code, an ordinance of a local government unit becomes effective as of the date the framers of such ordinance would like it to be effective and in the absence of such effectivity clause, the same shall take effect after ten (I O) days from the date a copy thereof is posted in a bulletin board at the entrance of the municipal hall and in at least two (2) other conspicuous places in the local government unit concerned." Accordingly, the pending issuance of an IRR, or the non-issuance thereof, cannot defer an ordinance coming into force. Further, perusal of the subject ordinance in question, there is no provision therein which prohibits its implementation sans an IRR. 1 HAGONOY MARKET VFNDOR ASSOCIATION vs. MUNICIPALITY OF HAGONOY. RUVACAN (G.R. NO. 137621)

Notwithstanding the foregoing, we respectfully reiterate that only the competent court has the authority to decide on the legality of an ordinance upon the initiation of appropriate action such as a petition for declaration of nullity of the ordinance. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, By t e Authority of the Secretary: cc: LLLS/27 MA DIRECTOR ARNEL M. AGABE Regional Director, DILG-Region X Masterson Ave., Upper Carmen Cagayan de Oro City INGAN, CESO Ill ry for Local Government
